hook: I just got a **legal notice.** Do I have to reply?
hook_q: What is a legal notice, and must I reply?

slides.title: First, check **which law** it cites.
slides.body: Some laws require a written notice before a case can be filed, and they set fixed deadlines. What happens next depends on the law behind the notice.

slides.title: Suing the **government?** Notice first.
slides.body: No suit can be filed against the Government, or a public officer over an official act, until two months after a written notice is delivered.
slides.note: urgent case? court may allow skipping it

slides.title: Ignore a cheque notice? **Risky.**
slides.body: If the drawer does not pay within 15 days of receiving the notice, it can be an offence: jail up to two years, or a fine up to twice the cheque amount, or both.

slides.title: Police notice? **Comply** with it.
slides.body: When arrest isn't required, police issue a notice to appear. If you comply, you shall not be arrested for that offence unless police record reasons. Not complying can lead to arrest.

caption:
Got a legal notice? What it means depends on the law behind it. 👇

1️⃣ Before suing the Government or a public officer over an official act, a written notice and a two-month wait are required
2️⃣ That notice must state the cause of action, your details and the relief claimed
3️⃣ Bounced cheque: the payee must send a written demand within 30 days of hearing from the bank
4️⃣ The drawer then has 15 days to pay. If not, it can be an offence with up to 2 years' jail, a fine up to twice the cheque amount, or both
5️⃣ A police notice to appear must be complied with. Not complying can lead to arrest
6️⃣ Whether and how to reply depends on the notice, so get legal advice quickly

Source: CPC, 1908 (Sec 80); Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 (Sec 138, 142); BNSS, 2023 (Sec 35)
